title: Beliefs & Foundations
description: Little Muslim → Beginner. Short questions introducing Allah, Islam, prophets, angels, the Quran and life after death, with simple meanings and familiar everyday examples. Written with children around ages 6–9 in mind; an adult may read questions aloud. All questions are Beginner level within the Kids audience.
levelMethod: Beginner describes the knowledge and understanding needed across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Uses introductory belief knowledge, short wording and straightforward examples for the Kids audience. Age and level are editorial guidance, not calibrated with children's reading or response data. Quiz performance describes learning needs, not a child's faith or worth.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original child-friendly educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Everyday scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval or a completed review with children.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Who created us and the world around us?
questions.explanation: Allah is the Creator of everything, including people, animals and plants.

questions.question: How many gods do Muslims believe in?
questions.explanation: Muslims believe in one God: Allah.

questions.question: To whom do Muslims offer their worship?
questions.explanation: We worship Allah alone. The things He created are not gods.

questions.question: Who needs Allah's care?
questions.explanation: Everyone needs Allah. Allah does not need anyone or anything.

questions.question: What does the Quran teach about Allah?

options.text: He hears only in a mosque
He needs a camera to see

questions.explanation: Allah is All-Hearing and All-Seeing. His hearing and seeing are not limited like ours.

questions.question: Who knows even the thoughts we have not shared?
questions.explanation: Allah knows what is spoken and what is hidden.

questions.question: Which word describes Allah in Surah Al-Fatihah?
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah teaches us that Allah is full of mercy.

questions.question: What do we ask Allah for in Al-Fatihah?
questions.explanation: We ask Allah to guide us to the right path.

questions.question: Who gives us rain that helps our food grow?
questions.explanation: Allah provides rain and helps crops and fruit grow.

questions.question: How should we respond to Allah's blessings?
questions.explanation: The Quran teaches us to remember Allah and be thankful to Him.

questions.question: What do we call asking Allah for help?
questions.explanation: Dua means calling upon Allah. We can turn to Him with our needs.

questions.question: What is the name of the religion Muslims follow?
questions.explanation: Islam is our religion. Arabic is a language, Makkah is a city, and Ramadan is a month.

questions.question: What did Allah's messengers teach people to do?
questions.explanation: Allah sent messengers to teach people to worship Him.

questions.question: Who is Allah's final prophet?
questions.explanation: Muhammad ﷺ is Allah's final prophet. The other names are also prophets, who came before him.

questions.question: Which book is Allah's message that Muslims read?
questions.explanation: The Quran comes from Allah and teaches us His message.

questions.question: Whom do the angels obey?
questions.explanation: Angels do what Allah commands them to do.

questions.question: Which of Allah's messengers do Muslims believe in?

options.text: Only those whose names we know

questions.explanation: Muslims believe in all the messengers Allah sent.

questions.question: Who can bring people back to life after death?
questions.explanation: Allah created us the first time and can bring us to life again.

questions.question: Which statement about Allah is true?

options.text: Allah forgets every small good deed
Allah judges by the price of our clothes

questions.explanation: Allah is never unfair, and even a small good deed matters to Him.

questions.question: When trying to do something useful, what should we do?

options.text: Wait for others to do everything
Try our best and ask Allah for help

questions.explanation: The Prophet taught us to seek what helps us and ask Allah for help.

questions.question: What does calling Allah our Creator mean?

options.text: He made us and all creation
He only made things we can hold
He made only our own town

questions.explanation: Allah created everything. His creation is much bigger than what we see nearby.

questions.question: What does Allah being One teach us?

options.text: Each town has its own god
There is no other god beside Him
Every family needs a different god

questions.explanation: Allah is One. We do not believe in many gods.

questions.question: Why do we not worship the sun?

options.text: It is too bright to name

questions.explanation: The sun is part of creation. Our worship is for Allah, the Creator.

questions.question: Do we need Allah only when something goes wrong?

options.text: Yes, only when we feel hungry

questions.explanation: Our need for Allah continues in happy times and difficult times.

questions.question: Does Allah need a lamp to see what happens?

options.text: No, Allah sees without needing one
Yes, only a lamp in a mosque
Yes, only a lamp at home

questions.explanation: Allah is All-Seeing. His seeing does not depend on light or equipment.

questions.question: Does Allah know only the things we say aloud?

options.text: No, He also knows what is hidden
Yes, only words said at school
Yes, only words on a stage

questions.explanation: Allah's knowledge includes our hidden thoughts as well as our spoken words.

questions.question: What does Allah's mercy teach us when we make a mistake?

options.text: We must stop trying to improve
We should never ask for help
We can turn back and ask forgiveness

questions.explanation: Allah teaches us not to lose hope in His mercy. We can return to Him and improve.

questions.question: What does asking Allah for guidance mean?

options.text: Asking never to listen to anyone
Asking Him to help us follow what is right

questions.explanation: Guidance helps us follow what is right, rather than simply get every wish.

questions.question: How is rain a blessing from Allah?

options.text: It gives water and helps plants grow
It means plants need no care
It turns every stone into food
It removes our need for water

questions.explanation: The Quran points to rain and growing plants as signs of Allah's care and provision.

questions.question: Does being thankful matter only for big gifts?

options.text: Yes, only prizes at school count

questions.explanation: The instruction to thank Allah is not limited to large or expensive blessings.

questions.question: Can a child call upon Allah in dua?

options.text: Yes, children can make dua too

questions.explanation: We can all turn to Allah in dua, including children.

questions.question: Is Islam only for people from one country?

options.text: Yes, only people from one city
Yes, only people from one island
Yes, only people living near us
No, people from many countries can follow Islam

questions.explanation: Allah sent His Messenger to all people, not just to one country.

questions.question: Why did Allah send messengers?

options.text: To guide people to worship Him
To teach people to worship toys
To make every person a king
To tell people not to learn

questions.explanation: The messengers brought Allah's message and called people to worship Him.

questions.question: What does final prophet mean?

options.text: A new prophet comes every year
No new prophet comes after Muhammad ﷺ

questions.explanation: Muhammad ﷺ is the last prophet. There will not be another prophet after him.

questions.question: Why is the Quran different from a made-up storybook?

options.text: It is only for decorating shelves
It is only a list of people's names
It is a message from Allah
It is a game made by a class

questions.explanation: The Quran is from Allah. We learn it to understand His message.

questions.question: Which statement about angels is right?

options.text: They are gods we should worship
They choose people to worship instead of Allah
They teach us to worship the moon
They worship Allah and obey Him

questions.explanation: Angels are servants of Allah, not gods. They worship and obey Him.

questions.question: Do Muslims reject earlier messengers because Muhammad ﷺ is the last prophet?

options.text: No, we believe in them too
Yes, we reject every earlier messenger
Yes, we believe in only our favorite one
Yes, we believe only if friends agree

questions.explanation: Believing in the final prophet does not mean rejecting the other messengers Allah sent.

questions.question: What does believing in life after death mean?

options.text: People become characters in a game
Allah will bring people to life again
Everyone becomes a star in the sky
Buildings give people a new life

questions.explanation: Allah tells us that the One who first created people will bring them to life again.

questions.question: Does a small good deed matter to Allah?

options.text: No, only very expensive deeds count
No, only famous people can do good
Yes, even a small good deed matters
No, only deeds seen by a crowd count

questions.explanation: Allah is never unfair and rewards good. A kind act does not need a large audience.

questions.question: Does trusting Allah mean we should stop making an effort?

options.text: Yes, someone else must do all our work
No, we ask for help and keep trying

questions.explanation: The Prophet's teaching joins seeking Allah's help with doing what is useful.

questions.question: Aminah sees birds, trees and clouds. What can she remember?
questions.explanation: The things we notice in nature can remind us that Allah is the Creator.

questions.question: Yusuf is learning Al-Ikhlas. Which sentence matches its teaching?

options.text: Each country has a separate god

questions.explanation: Al-Ikhlas teaches us that Allah is One.

questions.question: A friend asks, Do Muslims pray to the moon? What is the right answer?

options.text: Yes, only when it is full

questions.explanation: The moon is part of Allah's creation. Our worship is for Allah alone.

questions.question: Hasan learns a new skill. Does he now stop needing Allah?

options.text: Yes, learning one skill is enough

questions.explanation: Learning and success are blessings. They do not remove our need for Allah.

questions.question: Maryam helps someone when no other person is watching. Who still sees her kindness?

options.text: Only a person in the same room
Only someone looking through a window

questions.explanation: Allah is All-Seeing, so a kind act is not hidden from Him.

questions.question: Ali quietly plans a kind surprise. What is true about Allah's knowledge?

options.text: Allah knows it only after a teacher hears
Allah knows his plan before he tells people
Allah knows it only when it is written
Allah knows it only after a photograph

questions.explanation: Allah knows what is hidden as well as what we tell other people.

questions.question: Aminah made a mistake and wants to do better. What can she remember?

options.text: She should stop learning good habits
She must hide every mistake forever
She can ask Allah's forgiveness and try to improve

questions.explanation: Allah's mercy gives us hope to return to Him and do better.

questions.question: Yusuf wants help choosing what is right. Which dua fits?

options.text: Make every friend agree with me

questions.explanation: Asking Allah for guidance means seeking His help to follow the right path.

questions.question: Rain waters the family's vegetable garden. What can they remember?

options.text: Allah provides rain that helps food grow
Rain means the plants need no care
The watering can created the rain

questions.explanation: The Quran connects Allah's rain with the crops and fruit that help feed us.

questions.question: After enjoying a meal, what can Zaynab say to praise Allah?

options.text: I have nothing to be thankful for

questions.explanation: Alhamdulillah praises Allah. Food is one of the blessings for which we can be thankful.

questions.question: Before a school activity, what is one way Adam can turn to Allah?

options.text: Pretend only grown-ups can make dua
Wait until he is a teacher
Think Allah hears only in a mosque

questions.explanation: Adam can call upon Allah. Dua is not limited to grown-ups or one building.

questions.question: Maryam is talking about her religion. Which name should she use?
questions.explanation: Islam is the name of her religion, rather than a language, city or month.

questions.question: A lesson says Allah sent messengers. What did they invite people to do?

options.text: Make the sun into a god

questions.explanation: Allah's messengers taught people to worship Allah, not the messengers themselves.

questions.question: Yusuf makes a card about our final prophet. Which name belongs on it?
questions.explanation: Muhammad ﷺ is Allah's final prophet. Learning his name helps us know our Messenger.

questions.question: Aminah starts Quran lessons. What is a good reason for learning it?

options.text: Only to show off to friends
To avoid understanding any of it

questions.explanation: We learn the Quran because it is from Allah and teaches us His message.

questions.question: A class is learning about angels. Which sentence belongs in their notes?

options.text: Angels tell us to worship toys
Angels need people to worship them
Angels worship Allah and obey Him

questions.explanation: The Quran describes angels submitting to Allah and doing what He commands.

questions.question: A class learns about messengers sent before Muhammad ﷺ. How should Muslims think of them?

options.text: We believe in all Allah's messengers
We reject them because they came earlier
We believe only in the most familiar name
We accept them only if classmates vote for them

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches belief in all Allah's messengers, including those who came before the final prophet.

questions.question: A teacher asks who can bring people to life again. Which answer fits the Quran?

options.text: Allah, who created them the first time
The tallest tree in a garden

questions.explanation: Allah's power to create also reminds us of His power to bring people back to life.

questions.question: A child does a small kind deed that nobody praises. Does it still matter to Allah?

options.text: No, it needs a large audience
No, it must cost a lot of money
Yes, a small good deed still matters
No, only a famous person's kindness counts

questions.explanation: Allah does not overlook good because it is small or because people did not praise it.

questions.question: Aminah finds her reading practice difficult. What fits the Prophet's teaching?

options.text: Refuse every offer of useful help
Believe that making an effort never matters
Ask Allah for help and keep practicing

questions.explanation: Seeking Allah's help goes together with useful effort, including patient practice.
